title: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction

details.title: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction
details.abstract: Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) extends residual connections to multiple streams and stabilizes residual propagation by constraining stream-mixing residual matrices to the Birkhoff polytope, the set of doubly stochastic matrices. In this work, we investigate how to effectively mix residual streams within the Birkhoff polytope . We reveal a mixing trade-off : when under-mixed residual matrices stay close to the vertices of the Birkhoff polytope, hyper-connections will degenerate into a set of nearly independent streams; when over-mixe d residual matrices are concentrated around the uniform barycenter of the polytope, streams will become less distinguishable from each other. We theoretically validate our findings by bounding the cumulative residual mixing, stream difference and gradient difference of mixing coefficients across layers. Motivated by these findings, we propose Contraction for Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (cmHC), an exact doubly stochastic method which geometrically contracts the Birkhoff polytope toward its interior. This contraction mitigates under-mixing by forcing the residual matrices to explore deeper into the polytope, with a provable stream mixing bound and no new parameterization. Moreover, we apply a moderate contraction at the shallow layers to prevent over-mixing, enabling stable gradient propagation on extremely large-scale model pretraining. Extensive experiments across dense and mixture-of-experts models at various parameter scales demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of cmHC. We also develop fused operators for cmHC on Ascend NPUs, reducing hyper-connection execution latency by up to 44.8%.

title: Non-penetrating World Models

details.title: Non-penetrating World Models
details.abstract: 🚧 World models can generate amazing worlds, but they still walk through walls! 👻 🎮 Today's video world models can generate impressive interactive environments, but they often fail to respect basic physical boundaries. For example, when you press W toward a wall, the model may simply walk straight through it! 💡 We introduce NoPeWorld , a lightweight framework that helps video world models stop at obstacles instead of walking through them . Interestingly, we find that world models already encode collision information in their hidden states. NoPeWorld leverages this information to prevent physical violations without retraining the entire world model. 📊 We also introduce NoPeBench , a benchmark for evaluating whether world models respect physical boundaries. 🚀 Check out our demos and open-source resources! 🌐 Project & Demos | 💻 Code | 🤗 Dataset | 📄 Paper

title: Reading the Unreadable: Text-Aware Image Super-Resolution Needs Reasoning

details.title: Reading the Unreadable: Text-Aware Image Super-Resolution Needs Reasoning
details.abstract: [TL;DR] Text-aware image super-resolution (TAISR) needs reasoning! Humans can often read badly degraded text by reasoning over context: a word repeated elsewhere in the image, neighboring numbers on a ruler, or a familiar logo. Super-resolution (SR) models rely on local visual evidence alone, so they struggle with exactly this kind of text. 🔍 ReasonText is a human-curated benchmark that separates reasoning-required text from locally recoverable text, paired with GTTCA , a recognition-based metric that measures text restoration without text-detection errors. Across 12 recent SR models, including TAISR models built for text, accuracy on reasoning-required text stays below 25%. 💡 RTC (Reasoning Transfer via Captioning) is a training-free plug-in. An MLLM reasons out the degraded text and writes it into the caption of a frozen text-conditioned SR model. RTC improves all six text-conditioned SR models we tested, especially on reasoning-required text (e.g., DiT4SR: 24.5% → 45.8%). Surprisingly, DiT4SR + RTC, a general real-world SR model, outperforms UniT + RTC, a TAISR model built on the same backbone with extra text-aware modules. This suggests that reasoning should be a core design axis for future TAISR. 🤗 Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Jasonleex1995/ReasonText 🌐 Project page: https://jasonleex1995.github.io/TAISR_needs_Reasoning/ 💻 Code: https://github.com/jasonleex1995/TAISR_needs_Reasoning 📍 Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. title: PURE: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multi-Granularity Multimodal Identity Matching

details.title: PURE: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multi-Granularity Multimodal Identity Matching
details.abstract: Hi HF community! 👋 I’m one of the authors of PURE. Same design, different color: should two product listings count as a match? The answer depends on whether we care about the underlying product design or the specific variant. We introduce PURE , a diagnostic benchmark built from real-world e-commerce matching pairs , with 1,457 multiple-choice questions verified by domain experts across 14 tasks. It examines four capabilities involved in multimodal identity matching: Perception, Understanding, Reasoning, and Evidence-grounded Judgment , with explicit distinctions between base-level and variant-level matching. A few interesting findings from our evaluation of 10 multimodal LLMs: Understanding scores highest on average, while evidence-grounded judgment scores lowest. Locating visual differences and applying variant-level matching rules remain challenging. Models can incorrectly report attribute conflicts between records that actually match. The pattern changes with granularity: most models recognize matching pairs more accurately than non-matching pairs at the base level, while the reverse holds at the variant level. We hope PURE helps the community identify weaknesses that aggregate matching accuracy can hide, and provides a useful testbed for improving multimodal grounding and matching. 📊 Dataset and evaluation code We’d love to hear your thoughts and see how your models perform!

title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control

details.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
details.abstract: 🤖 Can frontier agents control robots directly with low-level actions? And how do we actually tell how good they are? 📉 Existing evaluations focus on episode-level scores such as success rates. They hide the action-level feedback that is key to improving embodied agents! 💡 We introduce AgentRoboCritic . The policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates every action against it. For a failed action, the critic also returns its failure mode. With GPT-6 Astra as the critic, we annotate 12,844 actions across 12 manipulation benchmarks. 🔍 What the action-level feedback reveals: Closed-loop recovery: 49.8% of successful episodes contain at least one failed action, and 57.7% of failed actions are recovered by the end of the episode. Reliable semantic grounding: acting on the wrong object, order or category accounts for only 0.2% of failed actions. Strong zero-shot manipulation: GPT-6 Astra succeeds in 91% of RoboTwin 2.0 and 90% of YAMLab episodes, where π0.5 reaches 6% and 0%. The remaining bottleneck is physical execution: Grasp is the leading failure mode on most benchmarks. 🚀 To make action-level feedback low-cost, we release the 12,844 annotated actions, a 400-action human-annotated benchmark, and a fine-tuned Muse-Glimmer-30B critic. Its failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.6% to 74.2%, at over 30× lower cost than GPT-6 Astra. 🌐 Project page | 💻 Code | 🤗 Dataset | 📊 Benchmark | 🧠 Critic model | 📄 Paper

title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step

details.title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step
details.abstract: We release ViDecide: Teaching video diffusion models to reason and plan step by step , which explores whether video diffusion models can reason and plan step by step, like the way language models do. Current video models often break physical or logical rules in multi-step reasoning and planning, even when the final frame looks right. We trace this to the conventional training paradigm, which generates a solution as one fixed-length clip instead of a chain of decisions. ViDecide makes three changes: 🧩 Causal generation with adaptive termination : the model generates one state transition at a time and decides when to stop with a visual EOS frame. 🎯 Decision-focused training schedule : training focuses on high noise levels, where the next move is decided. 🔁 Corrective Fine-tuning (CFT) : a new post-training method for autoregressive video diffusion. It maps the noise of a failed decision to the model's own successful continuation, avoiding the inaccurate credit assignment and unstable policy gradients of diffusion RL. On rule-based games (VideoRLVR), multi-step planning tasks (VBVR), and our new robot benchmark RoboTwin-Plan, ViDecide reaches an average strict success rate of 83.8% , vs. 23.3% for standard fine-tuning and 67.8% for the strongest prior method, and generalizes to larger puzzles and unseen layouts. Code, models, and data are open-sourced: 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26389 🌐 Project page: https://kevin-thu.github.io/ViDecide 💻 Code: https://github.com/Kevin-thu/ViDecide A ⭐ or an upvote would mean a lot, and we'd love to hear your thoughts! 🙏

title: GameAnything: From Any Inspirations to Playable Game Worlds

details.title: GameAnything: From Any Inspirations to Playable Game Worlds
details.abstract: GameAnything: From Any Inspirations to Playable Game Worlds AI-driven game development holds the potential to transform diverse human inspirations into interactive experiences. However, existing systems and benchmarks primarily focus on explicit development specifications, with limited support for adapting multimodal references and evaluating actual gameplay experiences. We introduce GameAnything , an open-source agentic platform that transforms multimodal inspirations into playable extensions of existing games through iterative development. GameAnything integrates coding agents with an independent playtesting critic, persistent development state, and reusable experience memory to support continuous refinement. We further present GameAnything-Bench , a benchmark spanning diverse reference modalities, game creation objectives, and gaming environments, with exploratory gameplay testing to assess both functional correctness and gameplay quality. Evaluations of nine coding agent configurations reveal that current agents can adapt reference content but still struggle with playable interactions and precise modifications. Moreover, multimodal references improve content fidelity, while iterative refinement yields substantial but varying improvements across agents. These findings highlight both the potential and remaining challenges of inspiration-driven game development.

title: WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce

details.title: WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce
details.abstract: We present WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal large language models that deliver frontier e-commerce capabilities while achieving state-of-the-art general-purpose performance at their respective scales. The family spans five sizes, from a 0.8B dense model to a 35B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters. Our training pipeline begins with two-stage continued pre-training that progressively raises the proportion of e-commerce data within a diverse multimodal data mixture, followed by hybrid-thinking post-training that combines on-policy distillation and reinforcement learning to support both non-thinking and thinking modes. For evaluation, we construct a comprehensive suite of 28 e-commerce benchmarks (23 in-house and five open-source) covering eight business scenarios and complement it with 64 public general-purpose benchmarks. On the e-commerce suite, WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B surpasses substantially larger open-source flagship models, including Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, HY4, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. On the general-purpose suite, every WeMM-Ecom model surpasses its similarly sized Qwen3.5 counterpart, with the lightweight variants (e.g., WeMM-Ecom-2B) showing clear advantages over leading lightweight models such as Qwen3.5-2B, MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B, and LFM3-VL-2B. Beyond benchmarks, WeMM-Ecom now powers hundreds of production use cases in WeChat, including catalog management, multimodal product search, and livestream commerce, serving billion-scale requests per day. We publicly release all model weights and detail our data curation, training recipe, and benchmark construction to facilitate future work on domain-specialized multimodal models.

title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation

details.title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation
details.abstract: Pretrained vision is a common start for robot learning, but most comparisons still score one pooled vector from a third-person image. Bimanual policies instead read dense patch tokens from cameras on the robot. We introduce HIVE-Bench: one shared flow-matching policy reads 20 encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual tasks, across adaptation, task sharing, and sweeps of data, model size, and layer. Keeping the patches matters. Averaging each view to one token removes most of the success, adaptation helps every pair we test, and one shared policy keeps most of the success of separate policies at a fraction of the updates. The same tokens are then scored with statistics, state and object readouts, published vision scores, and an inverse-dynamics readout. That readout of the commanded motion is one of the strongest measurements available before a policy is trained. Recognition, depth, and correspondence do not transfer reliably. Fine-tuning can improve the action readout even when other measurements move the other way, and no statistic is stable enough to replace a rollout before any deployment.

details.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
details.abstract: Can a robot improve across attempts while its model parameters stay frozen? In Embodied-Harness , we explore recursive self-improvement (RSI) for robotic manipulation. The Actor follows operational guidance to carry out a task. After a failed attempt, the Reflector uses the execution trace and prior experience to diagnose what went wrong and revise that guidance. The Actor then tries again with the revised guidance, and the new execution trace informs the next round of reflection. Embodied-Harness achieves success rates of 82.4% on RoboTwin 2.0 , 76.7% on RoboSPA , and 94.4% on RMBench . On three real-world manipulation tasks, it achieves an average success rate of 96.7% .

title: A Pipeline-Parallel System for Depth-Recurrent Models

details.title: A Pipeline-Parallel System for Depth-Recurrent Models
details.abstract: Depth-recurrent (Looped) models raise effective depth by applying a shared stack of blocks several times. Scaling them usually requires pipeline parallelism, but commonly used interleaved 1F1B is drawn for an acyclic stage graph in which each micro-batch enters each stage once. Once that stack is split across stages, the same stage is visited several times on one micro-batch and later stages feed earlier ones: native 1F1B has no slot for the extra visit, cannot rank a first iteration against a second, and its neighbour-only send/receive order has no back edge to the first stage, so the arrangement stalls or fires out of order. We present Loop-PP, which rebuilds both the timetable and the communication for this cyclic layout. It schedules different iterations of the same stage separately, specializes a 1F1B skeleton into a globally consistent order over those visits, and emits a static instruction stream per rank that separates posting from waiting so communication overlaps local compute. Loop-PP is bit-identical to a single-stage reference. On 8B-60B MoE models, it lowers peak memory by as much as 32.8%, and with compute budget fixed, the best observed throughput rises by 12.7%.

title: NoHairCache: Calibrate-Once KV Cache Eviction with One Power-Law Exponent

details.title: NoHairCache: Calibrate-Once KV Cache Eviction with One Power-Law Exponent
details.abstract: The decay exponent α in KV-cache eviction is an intrinsic property of the model: calibrated once on a single corpus, it transfers directly across domains. Attention-based accumulation (H2O) and recency-based sliding windows (StreamingLLM) are two dominant eviction frameworks, often treated as unrelated, but we show that they are the two endpoints of a single power-law family: by scoring each token as si=Ai⋅(t−i)−α, where Ai is cumulative attention and α controls the age penalty, H2O and StreamingLLM correspond to α=0 and α→∞, respectively (with StreamingLLM additionally hard-coding an attention-sink patch). The no-hair mechanism of \citet{xiang2026nohair} bounds the admissible range of α, and the measured exponents agree: calibrating once on WikiText yields [0.556,0.822] for a representative model (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct). The per-model ranges are consistent across five models (410M--1.5B) and independently match the optimal regions from perplexity sweeps. \textsc{NoHairCache} achieves the lowest perplexity across three datasets (WikiText, PG19, and arXiv) without per-dataset tuning, outperforming both H2O and StreamingLLM (p<0.05 on all three datasets, with 0.06--0.10 PPL gains over StreamingLLM at budget 512). On downstream four-way multiple-choice QA, it matches or outperforms StreamingLLM across all nine (task, budget) cells, retaining 98.2% of full-cache accuracy on NarrativeQA at 25% retention versus 91.1% for StreamingLLM; per-cell McNemar tests are not significant, so QA is corroborating only. We release our calibration script and drop-in scorer upon publication.

title: Beyond Attention Maps: Understanding and Improving Medical MLLMs via Visual Values

details.title: Beyond Attention Maps: Understanding and Improving Medical MLLMs via Visual Values
details.abstract: Are We Overlooking the V in MLLMs Attention? Most existing studies on MLLMs focus on improving spatial attention — teaching models where to look. But does looking at the right region necessarily lead to a correct answer? In our recent work, Beyond Attention Maps: Understanding and Improving Medical MLLMs via Visual Values, we revisit this question using paired non-contrast and contrast-enhanced medical images. Our findings reveal that: 🔹 Highly similar attention maps can lead to drastically different predictions. 🔹 Intervening on visual values (V) produces substantially larger prediction changes than intervening on attention weights. 🔹 Informative visual values remain beneficial even when attention maps are heavily perturbed. Motivated by these observations, we propose VIVID, a visual value-guided on-policy distillation framework that uses the student's response to enhanced visual evidence to refine teacher supervision. Beyond medical imaging, we hope to inspire a broader discussion: Should we shift some of our attention from learning where to look towards learning what to retrieve? And for on-policy distillation, should we focus not only on what the teacher predicts, but also on how visual evidence shapes its supervision? 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29361 🌐 Project: https://qiuzyc.github.io/VIVID We welcome discussions and feedback from the community! #MLLM #VisualUnderstanding #Attention #OnPolicyDistillation #MedicalAI

title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?

details.title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?
details.abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents are widely trained in executable GUI environments. To lower cost, build environments in batches, and reduce manual effort, each work trades away part of the environment through its construction choices. We describe these choices along three dimensions: reward coverage, the goal-reaching trajectories the verifier rewards; data coverage, the application data the agent is exposed to beyond what the task reads or writes; and feature coverage, the application features beyond what the task uses. Existing works set each dimension on engineering grounds, but they do not measure its effect on training. How complete must an environment be to train a capable agent, and along which dimensions? In MobileGym, we adjust each dimension separately, train Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, and evaluate every policy in the original full environment. A verifier that rewards only one reference path lowers success by 10.53 points, and removing unneeded records also lowers success. Pruning unneeded features instead raises success from 51.61% to 56.13%, entirely on tasks whose environments it left unchanged. The gain reverses when each episode is weighted equally and vanishes when only episodes on the pruned tasks are balanced. Without pruning, length weighting there reinforces long detour successes that erode skills on other tasks. Following these findings, we build MobileGym-Lite, which keeps reward and data coverage complete and prunes unneeded features. It outperforms Full in the full environment (55.48% versus 51.61% success) with lower construction cost.

title: ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control

details.title: ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control
details.abstract: We are introducing ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents as Policy . A robot policy built from persistent coding agents that reason and act asynchronously. A single coding agent can issue parallel motion commands, but every decision still passes through one reasoning process. While it diagnoses a grasp with one arm, independent work on the other may wait. ACAP distributes decision-making across parts of one robot, with a hyper-agent coordinating their work. 🦾 Each member is a robot policy. A persistent agent controls a configurable group, such as an arm with its gripper or the torso and chassis. It observes, reasons, writes control code, acts and uses feedback to decide its next step. Members' reasoning and execution can overlap. 🧭 Let an agent coordinate the policies. The hyper-agent decides what to delegate, when members synchronize, and when the lead should directly control several parts. Members prepare flowers in parallel and take turns at the vase. For a shared towel fold, the lead controls both arms. Coordination comes from observations and feedback, without a hand-written script. ⚡ Lower time cost on real robots. Across 72 rollouts in 25 task/platform settings on Galaxea R1 Pro and AgileX PiPER-family robots, ACAP cuts task-balanced time cost by 28.2% versus a single-agent Direct Policy. It also has lower mean time cost than Fixed Delegation, where control always stays with members, on all eight collaborative settings, and than Direct on all six tasks of a separate 90-rollout repeated study. 🧮 From observations to geometry to action. Frontier coding agents control the robot through geometry they compute in code while the task is running. They model the scene, derive a motion, act and check how the object responds. An agent triangulates a thin flower tip by moving its hand, turns a fitted bottle axis into a corrective wrist rotation, and tracks carton features to overturn a mistaken slip diagnosis. 📦 162 real-world rollouts for research. The dataset preserves this behavior, linking observations, generated programs, numerical results, agent messages, actions and robot feedback. Researchers can trace how agents build representations, turn calculations into commands, and revise decisions from physical evidence. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31205 🌐 Project page: https://projects.zxhezexin.com/acap 🤗 Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/zxhezexin/acap-rollout-dataset We'd love to hear your thoughts. title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention

details.title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
details.abstract: Hi everyone! Author here — happy to share LoomFormer , along with our JAX/Pallas training code, PyTorch/Triton inference kernels, and 300B-token 2.8B checkpoints (including a matched mHC-Pythia-2.8B baseline). TL;DR: Why layer-wise residual routing hits a ceiling: Recent residual-stream mechanisms ( HC/mHC , AttnRes , MUDDFormer ) share routing ports across all heads of a layer, restricting their head-to-head wiring matrix to rank ≤ 1 (or ≤ 3 in MUDDFormer). Per-token head-to-head rewiring: LoomFormer generates ports per head and per token via normalized and gated linear attention ( MRead / MWrite ) over a fixed per-token matrix memory M_t of shape [d_k, d] , reaching wiring rank 2n in a smaller per-token state ( 3D ) than 4-stream HC/mHC ( 4D ). Scaling & 300B pretraining: Matches Transformers trained with >3× compute across scales. Trained on 300B Pile tokens with only +1.95% FLOPs , LoomPythia-2.8B achieves 1.6× the downstream gain of mHC-Pythia-2.8B , matches Pythia-12B in 0-shot ( 59.9 ), and surpasses Pythia-12B in 5-shot ( 61.6 vs. 60.8 ) and FLAN ppl ( 6.94 vs. 7.26 ), while lifting deep non-sink active heads from ~20% to 74.4% . Wall-clock speed: Sustains 89–92% of Transformer training speed on TPU v5p (fused Pallas kernels) and 84–92% of prefill/decode speed on GPU (fused Triton + CUDA graphs). Links: Code (JAX/Pallas + PyTorch/Triton): https://github.com/Caiyun-AI/LoomFormer LoomPythia-2.8B (300B tokens): https://huggingface.co/Caiyun-AI/LoomPythia-2.8B mHC-Pythia-2.8B (300B baseline): https://huggingface.co/Caiyun-AI/mHC-Pythia-2.8B Happy to answer any questions on the circuit theory, ablations, or kernels!

title: PartAgent: Agentic 3D Part Segmentation via Expert Integration and Closed-Loop Refinement

details.title: PartAgent: Agentic 3D Part Segmentation via Expert Integration and Closed-Loop Refinement
details.abstract: We present PartAgent, a training-free agentic framework for 3D part segmentation built upon two complementary modules: (i) Structural–Semantic Expert Integration combines regions predicted by the 3D expert with multiview semantic evidence from the 2D expert through image-to-surface correspondences, constructing compositional part partitions at multiple granularities. (ii) Observation-Driven Closed-Loop Partition Refinement observes the current partition and its supporting evidence to select targeted inspection, evidence repair, composition, or reselection actions. It verifies proposed changes and uses the updated state and action outcomes to guide subsequent decisions. On PartObjaverse-Tiny-WT, PartAgent achieves 68.41 mIoU, outperforming the strongest competing method by 8.53 points. Across 3DCoMPaT200, PartNeXt, PartNetE, and PartObjaverse-Tiny, PartAgent achieves the highest mIoU on each dataset, averaging 69.36 on the four datasets, 7.28 points above the highest mean among competing methods. title: S-Mind: Internalizing Multi-View Geometry for Spatial Intelligence

details.title: S-Mind: Internalizing Multi-View Geometry for Spatial Intelligence
details.abstract: Spatial intelligence, the ability to reason about 3D space from visual observations, becomes essential as multimodal large language models (MLLMs) move into the physical world. Beyond perceiving each view, it rests on two cornerstones of human cognition: fusing multiple views into one coherent 3D scene and mentally transforming that scene to new viewpoints as reasoning unfolds. Yet our spatial probes reveal that MLLMs largely lack both capabilities, even after spatial fine-tuning. We therefore present S-Mind, which internalizes multi-view geometry within the MLLM through a compact set of spatial tokens. It supervises these tokens to hold the fused 3D scene and re-emits them to re-express this scene from every viewpoint the reasoning adopts. title: PhyCoVE: Benchmarking Physical Counterfactual Video Editing across Diverse Material Dynamics

details.title: PhyCoVE: Benchmarking Physical Counterfactual Video Editing across Diverse Material Dynamics
details.abstract: 🔥 Can video editing models understand physics? Remove a stone before it drops into a full glass of water, and the water should never overflow. Make it heavier, and the splash should grow. A physical edit changes not only how a scene looks, but how it evolves afterward. We introduce PhyCoVE , a benchmark for physical counterfactual video editing across rigid, elastic, and fluid dynamics: 📊 533 cases on 110 source videos , each pairing a source video and a physical edit with a counterfactual target video 🧪 5 interaction patterns (rigid–rigid, rigid–elastic, rigid–fluid, elastic–fluid, elastic–elastic), in both simulated and real-recorded scenes ✂️ 3 edit types : remove an object (178), change a physical quantity (334), insert an object (21), with 63 edits taking effect at a later frame 📐 Counterfactual Fidelity (CF) : measures how much of the source-to-target physical change a generated video reproduces; it ranks models nearly as human preference does (Kendall τ = 0.90), while pixel metrics favor the unedited source Key findings on 7 models (MiniMax H3, Seedance 2.5, Wan 3.0, Kling 4.0, JoyAI, Kiwi-Edit, OmniWeaving): Even the best model reproduces only ~1/7 of the physical change (CF = 0.134): models change how a scene looks, but rarely how it evolves Parameter edits (mass, stiffness, density, flow rate) are essentially unsolved (top CF = 0.019) Premature execution : 44 of 63 later-frame removals happen before the requested frame 🌐 Project page: https://phycove.github.io/ 🤗 Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ccmoony/PhyCoVE 💻 Code: https://github.com/Hammour-steak/PhyCoVE

title: Reinforcing Diffusion Models by Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching

details.title: Reinforcing Diffusion Models by Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching
details.abstract: Hi everyone! 👋 Excited to share our new work iTDM (Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching) for reinforcing diffusion and flow-matching models! TL;DR: Existing forward diffusion RL methods (enabling fast deterministic ODE rollouts without trajectory backprop, e.g., DGPO, DiffusionNFT, AWM) essentially rely on signed Reward-Weighted Regression (RWR) centered at the policy velocity $v_\theta$. We show that subtracting a reward baseline in RWR implicitly assumes $v_\theta = v_q$ (the rollout behavior velocity)—an assumption violated under CFG rollouts, offline/off-policy updates, and imperfect self-consistency, causing baseline-induced gradient drift and coarse few-step rollout artifact fitting . How iTDM fixes this: By taking the infinitesimal step-size limit of Trajectory Distribution Matching (TDM) via the Gaussian posterior-score identity, iTDM yields an exact sample-level RL gradient anchored at the behavior velocity $v_q$— without training an extra reward-tilted score network. Tracking $v_q$ online with a lightweight auxiliary LoRA denoiser and regularizing toward the frozen reference guarantees exact baseline invariance at the auxiliary optimum, naturally unifying online and offline RL without drift or blurry artifacts. Key Highlights: ⚡ ~3× Faster & Collapse-Free Scaling: Reaches 0.75 nearly 3× faster than DGPO, DiffusionNFT, and AWM on GenEval2 (SD3.5-M), scaling smoothly to 0.87 without training collapse. 🎯 Unlocks Stable CFG-Guided Online & Offline RL: Leads CFG-guided online RL across compositional generation ( 0.97 GenEval), text rendering ( 0.96 OCR), and preference alignment ( 24.08 PickScore) on SD3.5-M, while overcoming offline collapse/divergence under frozen rollouts ( 0.87 GenEval, 0.92 OCR, 22.26 PickScore; outperforming Diffusion-DPO across all tasks at $G=2$)—preserving/improving 7 unseen DrawBench metrics without background collapse or blurry textures. 🚀 Scales to 5.6B FLUX.3 Klein Base: Guidance-free ( CFG=1.0 ) reinforcement with HPSv3++ surpasses even the CFG-guided base model ( CFG=3.5 ) across both in-domain and unseen quality/alignment metrics. 🔗 Links: 🌐 Project Page: https://luo-yihong.github.io/iTDM/ 💻 Code: https://github.com/Luo-Yihong/iTDM 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30986

title: AdProducer: Towards Agentic Advertising Video Generation

details.title: AdProducer: Towards Agentic Advertising Video Generation
details.abstract: Recent advances in video generation have made automated advertising production increasingly feasible. However, an effective advertisement must faithfully represent the product and communicate its selling points through compelling visual storytelling, which requires more than visual synthesis: it calls for deeper product understanding and strategic decisions about how to present product value. Crucially, product research and creative design are closely intertwined, as the information gathered about a product determines which features can be faithfully demonstrated and how they should be presented. In this paper, we introduce AdProducer, the first end-to-end agentic framework for advertising video creation, transforming concise creative briefs into finished advertisements. Our multimodal agent autonomously researches products through web and image search and translates its findings into selling-point-driven storyboards that guide a frozen video generator. To achieve this, we develop a dedicated data construction pipeline that yields two training datasets, AdProducer-SFT and AdProducer-RL, and train the agent through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning with joint optimization of storyboard- and video-level rewards. We further introduce AdCreation-Bench, comprising 305 advertising briefs across eight domains, with two complementary metrics: PG-Score for product correctness and creative execution, and Ad-Score for overall advertising effectiveness assessed by an independent judge. Experiments demonstrate that AdProducer improves the PG-Score of MiniMax H3 from 17.3 to 51.3 and generalizes to Veo 3.1 without additional training, improving its score from 28.0 to 35.9, with consistent gains in Ad-Score, VideoScore2, and human evaluations. title: Coding4Games: Can Modern Coding Agents Play Modern Video Games?

details.title: Coding4Games: Can Modern Coding Agents Play Modern Video Games?
details.abstract: Games, especially modern AAA games, challenge language models to perceive complex scenes, control actions, and make decisions over long horizons. Existing game benchmarks primarily test language models as computer-use agents that query a language model throughout play, incurring repeated inference cost and, in real-time games, acting while the environment continues to evolve. We ask whether coding agents can learn from game interaction to develop standalone game-playing programs that run without language-model inference. We thus introduce Coding4Games, a benchmark for evaluating whether coding agents can develop standalone programs that play modern games through visual observations and standard game inputs. Coding4Games has three defining features: 1) Diverse Modern Games, covering 15 games with diverse visual, strategic, and control demands; 2) Development–Test Separation, in which a coding agent uses a sandbox and the standard player interface to iteratively develop a program, after which the selected program is frozen and independently tested without language-model inference; and 3) Outcome and Process Evaluation, which measures not only game performance and reliability but also how agents use feedback, revise programs, and resolve problems during development. Across 15 games, the best program per game outscores the strongest GUI baseline on 13 and ties it on one. The human player outscores all agents on 10 games. We additionally examine the effects of development budgets. Coding4Games evaluates whether coding agents can turn their understanding of complex interactive environments into programs that work reliably on their own.

title: Can an Agent Trust Its Own Zoom? Cross-Magnification Provenance Verification for Whole-Slide Images

details.title: Can an Agent Trust Its Own Zoom? Cross-Magnification Provenance Verification for Whole-Slide Images
details.abstract: Visual agents navigate whole-slide images through magnified observations associated with claimed locations. However, a visually plausible observation does not necessarily originate from its claimed location, particularly across magnifications and in regions with similar tissue structures. We formulate cross-magnification provenance verification (CMPV) to evaluate whether visual evidence supports a claimed spatial association, recover the source when possible, and abstain when evidence is insufficient. We introduce PyraFault, a benchmark of 3.06 million coordinate-supervised examples from 2,200 cases across five TCGA cohorts, covering within-context substitutions, absent-source faults, and geometric perturbations. We further propose ZoomTrace, a claim-independent verifier that estimates the observation's source before evaluating its agreement with the claimed location. It combines physical-scale alignment, visual retrieval, geometric refinement, and reliability estimation using spatially disjoint competing matches. On 503,320 test examples, ZoomTrace achieves 0.969 AUPRC and 0.987 AUROC, compared with 0.789 and 0.903 for Efficient LoFTR. Further evaluations reveal trade-offs in reliability estimation and limitations in vision-language models, cross-dataset retrieval, and calibration. Integrating ZoomTrace into visual agent tool paths reduces exposure to corrupted observations and silent failures, while downstream accuracy improvements depend on the agent and verification threshold.

title: Do learned image captioning metrics generalize? Auditing duplicated samples in human-judgment benchmarks

details.title: Do learned image captioning metrics generalize? Auditing duplicated samples in human-judgment benchmarks
details.abstract: Hi everyone! We're excited to share our recent work: Do Learned Image Captioning Metrics Generalize? Auditing Duplicated Samples in Human-Judgment Benchmarks How reliable are the reported gains of learned image captioning metrics? To find out, we conducted a systematic audit of three recent human-judgment benchmarks: Polaris , Nebula , and Spica . Key Findings: Substantial Data Leakage: 68.4% of the Polaris test set appears verbatim in the Spica training set (identical images, captions, and human ratings). Memorization Over Generalization: Over five training epochs, Pearl's gain on duplicated samples jumps from 2.5 to 10.4 Kendall's τ points, while performance on non-duplicated samples remains virtually flat. Flawed Evaluation Signals: Much of the reported correlation is driven by spotting the lowest-rated captions, which masks differences in fine-grained ranking ability. Rethinking the Leaderboard: Under a leakage-controlled protocol, zero-shot VLM judges take the lead, while a simple ridge regression on frozen features matches or outperforms several complex learned metrics. To address these issues, we propose a more rigorous evaluation protocol, with broader implications for evaluators trained on human judgments. Resources & Reproducibility: 📄 Paper: arXiv:2611.30488 💻 Code & Tools: GitHub Repo (deduplication tools and reproduction scripts) 🤗 Data & Checkpoints: Hugging Face Dataset (model weights, 82 retrained checkpoints, and per-sample scores) Note: All 23 tables and 300 reported numbers can be reproduced on CPU only—no expensive GPUs required.

title: Escriba-OCR: A 1B Vision-Language Model for Error-Preserving Transcription of Handwritten Portuguese Essays

details.title: Escriba-OCR: A 1B Vision-Language Model for Error-Preserving Transcription of Handwritten Portuguese Essays
details.abstract: Escriba-OCR-1B is a 1B-parameter OCR model that transcribes handwritten Brazilian Portuguese essays exactly as the student wrote them: misspellings, line breaks, struck-through words and insertions included. Feedback tools and research on learner writing need that, but vision-language models tend to rewrite the text into correct Portuguese. Benchmark. 22 open baselines (0.8B to 400B parameters) on the 199 BRESSAY test pages, scored on CER plus error preservation, invented errors, edit-markup precision and recall, and line structure, with paired bootstrap confidence intervals. Every VLM replaces 39–78% of the words that are not in a Portuguese dictionary with dictionary words. Model. LightOnOCR-3-1B fine-tuned on 647 pages in 85 minutes on one GPU: 2.06% CER against 5.60% for the best baseline, Qwen3-VL 235B-A22B (95% CI of the difference [−4.2, −2.9]). It recovers 77% of illegible deletions and 67% of insertions, and gets the line structure right on 97% of the pages. Runs at school. Quantised to 4 bits, it transcribes a page in about a minute on an ordinary CPU, so the essays never leave the school's computers. Limits. It still normalises 60% of likely misspellings, and on 40 letters from another corpus it misreads words it never saw in training more often than its base model. A teacher's review finds that 45% of the judgeable apparent corrections are errors in the BRESSAY ground truth. details.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
details.abstract: Hi everyone! 👋 We are the Sage-Med Team , excited to share our paper: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence . TL;DR: We benchmarked 77 models across 238 clinical tasks (61 public + 13 private multi-center benchmarks from 14 hospitals and institutions, 40+ modalities) to diagnose why medical multimodal scaling stalls. Guided by these findings, we introduce Sage-Med-Preview (35B-A3B) , combining stage-specific six-step curation over 322.7M candidate records with medical pretraining, 3-stage progressive SFT, and adaptive GRPO reinforcement learning with difficulty sampling and independent reference replay. 🔍 Benchmarking Insights: The Visual Scaling Bottleneck Existing medical MLLMs still trail general-purpose MLLMs on 29 of 31 public multimodal benchmarks. Parameter scaling within a model family mainly improves text ( +9.90% text-only understanding, +12.37% text-only reasoning), while yielding much smaller gains on multimodal understanding ( +4.34% ). Enabling reasoning modes boosts text reasoning and knowledge, yet brings virtually no gain to visual perception ( 0.54% difference across 22 perception benchmarks) and can even weaken perception within the same backbone. 🚀 Model Performance & Preliminary Training Exploration Leading open-source multimodal performance: Achieves 58.26% across 31 public multimodal benchmarks (vs. 50.99% for Hulu-Med-235B-A22B and 52.24% for Intern-S2-Preview), 59.81% on 15 specialized benchmarks, and 80.05% on comprehensive multimodal understanding (ahead of GPT-6.2-Sol at 76.81%). Strong multi-center generalization: Ranks #1 overall on unseen private multi-center clinical benchmarks at 57.72% (vs. 51.24% for GPT-6.2-Sol). Preliminary pipeline ablations: We also share initial explorations and ablations on our training pipeline (pretraining data composition, base-model initialization, modality and response-length mixtures, and progressive SFT + adaptive RL), suggesting that supervision quality, modality balance, and curriculum design outweigh raw data volume alone. 🔗 Links: Website | Hugging Face | GitHub | Leaderboard We hope both the model and our empirical findings are useful to the community. title: AIRIS: Benchmarking Social Embodied Intelligence in Egocentric Streaming Videos

details.title: AIRIS: Benchmarking Social Embodied Intelligence in Egocentric Streaming Videos
details.abstract: Embodied agents operating around people must not only recognize social cues, but also decide when the available evidence is sufficient, whether to intervene, and how to respond without violating social norms. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate these abilities in isolation or with access to completed videos, obscuring where an online social decision fails. We introduce AIRIS, a causal streaming benchmark that formulates social embodied intelligence as a time-anchored chain of Attention, Intention, Reaction, and Interaction (A-I-R-I). AIRIS contains 8,000 expert-curated questions grounded in 357 egocentric clips across 11 context categories and 36 capability dimensions. At each query, models receive only the observation prefix available at that time; decision-aware metrics reward calibrated waiting and complete reactions while penalizing premature commitment. Evaluating 45 proprietary and open-source general-purpose, embodied, streaming-video, and omni-modal models reveals fragmented and temporally miscalibrated competence. General-purpose VLMs excel at passive cue grounding and intent recognition, whereas embodied specialists lead on isolated reaction sub-decisions; yet across all families, models frequently guess intents before sufficient evidence emerges and fail to jointly align intervention timing, action domain, and concrete execution within the same episode. AIRIS thus provides a diagnostic foundation for bridging the gap between passive social perception and reliable embodied interaction.

title: What Is Redundant at High Resolution? Efficient Attention and Feed-Forward Design for All-in-One Image Restoration

details.title: What Is Redundant at High Resolution? Efficient Attention and Feed-Forward Design for All-in-One Image Restoration
details.abstract: Hi everyone! 👋 I'm the first author of this paper. TL;DR: We ask what is actually redundant at high resolution in multi-scale all-in-one image restoration (AIO-IR) networks, and use the answer to build HiGLR , a fast and memory-efficient AIO-IR model. Our stage-wise analysis finds three redundancies, and each one leads to a design choice: Finest stage: what self-attention adds beyond uniform pooling is largely shared across queries → we replace it with a learned, input-independent kernel. Intermediate stages: neighboring queries select largely the same keys → Block-Routed Hybrid Attention (BRHA) shares routing indices across neighbors and combines coarse dense attention over block summaries with fine block-sparse attention over value residuals. ConvFFNs: spatial mixing tolerates much lower rank than the nonlinear expansion → Dual-Space FFN (DSFFN) does spatial mixing in a compact space and keeps the expanded part pointwise, enabling kernel fusion. With only 7M parameters, HiGLR achieves state-of-the-art results on AIO-3, AIO-5 and CDD-11, with up to 4.24× faster inference and 65.8% lower peak GPU memory than CEA-IR-S. title: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts

details.title: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
details.abstract: AI wearables, such as smart glasses, extend the context available to agents beyond digital environments to users' everyday physical surroundings. With these devices, computer tasks can originate from users' ongoing real-world activities rather than solely from explicit instructions. Through first-person observations, agents can identify objects and activities relevant to user requests and ground digital tasks in the surrounding context. We call this interaction paradigm Ego Use . However, first-person observations are limited by the wearer's viewpoint and may provide incomplete or ambiguous evidence of ongoing activities. As new observations arrive, agents may need to revise their understanding of the physical context and user intent, and reassess whether prior digital actions remain valid. Whether current agents can reliably handle these changes remains insufficiently evaluated. We introduce EgoUseBench , a benchmark for evaluating Ego Use across three interaction settings with different levels of first-person context. Computer-Use relies on explicit instructions, Offline Ego Use provides prerecorded first-person context before execution, and Online Ego Use provides continuous observations as user intent evolves. Based on over 74 hours of real-world first-person recordings, we construct 693 tasks across the three interaction settings. To capture task evolution, we track first-person observations, user requirements, and website state separately. We further group tasks by how information changes during execution, resulting in three types: Graft (revised user requirements), Refresh (new first-person observations), and Clarify (agent-initiated information seeking). We evaluate several advanced models and find that average success rates in Online Ego Use are 26.3% lower than in Computer-Use. This result reveals the difficulty of keeping task execution aligned with evolving first-person context and user intent.

title: Loupe: Reinforcing Knowledge-Intensive Video Generation Agents

details.title: Loupe: Reinforcing Knowledge-Intensive Video Generation Agents
details.abstract: We present Loupe, an agentic framework for knowledge-intensive video generation that addresses the challenges of missing factual knowledge, entity appearances, and temporal relationships in user prompts. Loupe autonomously leverages text search, image search, and web browsing to retrieve, verify, and integrate external evidence, producing factually grounded video prompts and visual references for downstream video generators. To enable effective agent training, we introduce Rubric-Based Credit (RBC), a process supervision framework that derives task-specific evaluation criteria directly from user requests and provides fine-grained, step-level feedback for search and planning decisions. Building on RBC, we develop RBC-SFT and RBC-GRPO, enabling effective supervised and reinforcement learning without requiring video rendering during training. We also introduce Search-VBench, a dedicated benchmark consisting of 150 prompts across seven categories for evaluating knowledge-intensive video generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements across multiple video generators, increasing MiniMax-H3's overall score from 32.80 to 70.67, highlighting the effectiveness of search augmentation and process supervision for knowledge-intensive video generation.

title: Beyond Code and Pixels: Co-Generating Editable and Visually Rich Presentations

details.title: Beyond Code and Pixels: Co-Generating Editable and Visually Rich Presentations
details.abstract: Generating PPTX presentations is a structured task that requires semantic planning, visual composition, precise layout, and editability, motivating collaboration among specialized agents. However, programmatic methods offer editability but often produce rigid designs, while image-based methods provide visual richness but flatten content into difficult-to-edit pixels. A hybrid system can combine these strengths, but must coordinate interdependent decisions across content, layout, and appearance. To address this challenge, we propose SlidesWeaver, a hybrid multi-agent system that coordinates language and vision agents through shared deck- and slide-level states. Specifically, it uses staged multimodal commitment, diffusion-based composition planning, and two generation schedules for different priorities between composition freedom and accurate text preservation, while preserving native text and geometry. Across 1,728 generations spanning 24 system-model configurations, SlidesWeaver achieves consistently superior overall quality across all evaluated dimensions while maintaining structural control, editability, and practical generation efficiency.

title: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation

details.title: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation
details.abstract: General-purpose multimodal foundation models enable robots to adapt during deployment from observations and execution feedback, without task-specific demonstrations or training. However, the robot retains what it learns only in the model's working context. Once the task ends, it loses this execution knowledge, such as how to carry a bowl between two grippers. On the next attempt at the task, the robot may take just as long and repeat the same mistakes. To avoid this repetition, robots must retain execution knowledge across attempts. Yet replaying past actions is insufficient, because their effects depend on the current conditions. Procedures that determine actions from the current scene address this, but when they meet conditions that earlier attempts did not cover, revising them requires the measured effects of earlier actions. We therefore propose SEEK, an agentic framework that retains both, enabling robots to improve across attempts while keeping the underlying model fixed. To adapt retained knowledge to the current scene, SEEK adopts a Self-Evolving Programmatic Policy (SEPP) that encodes manipulation as executable procedures and determines each action from current observations. As the robot executes these procedures, SEEK records the measured effects of its actions, including those from failed attempts, in a Persistent Action-Effect Bank (PAEB). Where a retained procedure applies, it acts without a model request; where it meets a condition it does not cover, this evidence guides its revision. On RoboDojo, knowledge retained over ten attempts raises SEEK's average task score from 27.0 to 54.4 and its success rate from 19.7% to 48.0% across all 42 tasks. On 34 of these tasks with GPT-6.2 Astra, SEEK reaches 80.1 after five attempts, against 49.6 for the same model acting directly, and uses 77.6% fewer model requests.

title: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time

details.title: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time
details.abstract: Most test-time methods for LLMs vote : sample independent answers and trust the majority, both to pick the final answer and to build training targets. That wastes earlier reasoning, and when the majority is wrong, training on it reinforces the error. TT-RSI (Test-Time Recursive Self-Improvement) lets the model build on its own previous attempts instead, with no labels: In-Context RSI (inference, training-free): re-solve each question with the full previous solution as a neutral reference; the model decides what to reuse, rework, or redo. In-Weight RSI (label-free test-time training): distills successive refinements into the weights via on-policy self-distillation (Recursive + Accelerated Distillation). Because it learns from refinement rather than agreement, it can move past a wrong majority. The two reinforce each other: the updated model refines better, producing stronger references for the next round. We also show that distilling just two successive solutions moves the first attempt toward the model's infinite-step refinement limit. Results : +13.89% average accuracy over the base model, and +4.79% over TTPO + SC, the strongest self-consistency method, at the same test-time budget. 🌐 Project page: https://uanu2002.github.io/TT-RSI/ 💻 Repo: https://github.com/uanu2002/TT-RSI

title: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures

details.title: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures
details.abstract: Robot world models are increasingly used to evaluate and plan policies, yet robot training data are dominated by successful demonstrations. Off the happy path, when a grasp is misaligned or mistimed and the object is pushed, tilted, or slips, their predictions break down. Across five pretrained action-conditioned models, object-motion error is at most 10.4% lower than that of a static baseline that copies the first frame, and two models are worse than this baseline. We present WorldReforge, which teaches world models what happens when manipulation goes wrong. We construct the Reforge dataset of 62k simulated trajectories by perturbing reference grasps in position, orientation, and closure timing, recording each resulting push, slip, or failed pickup with ground-truth object pose, contact, and surface points. WorldReforge turns this ground truth into two training signals without additional inference cost. Interaction Alignment focuses reconstruction on the small object and contact regions that a global loss underweights, and Surface Correspondence trains backbone features to follow the same physical surface points across frames. On Cosmos3 Nano, WorldReforge reduces object trajectory error by 28.2% overall and by 35.0% on unseen objects, and it lowers the error in predicting how two actions' outcomes diverge by 43.3%. Although trained only in simulation, it also improves reconstruction on DROID and on real failure videos. Controlled data studies show that failed contact and successful holding teach complementary physics: failed contact teaches how objects respond, and holding teaches how a grasped state persists. Our code, data, and models are available at https://github.com/aim-uofa/WorldReforge .

title: SPARC: Geometry-Guided Attention Pruning for Long-Horizon Camera-Controlled Video Generation

details.title: SPARC: Geometry-Guided Attention Pruning for Long-Horizon Camera-Controlled Video Generation
details.abstract: We present SPARC, a geometry-guided attention pruning framework that turns the native self-attention of pretrained video diffusion transformers into a unified mechanism for camera control and persistent scene memory. Our key insight is that attention connectivity can simultaneously serve as geometric conditioning for camera control and spatial addressing for historical memory retrieval. Motivated by the asymmetric contextual requirements of reconstructing observed content and synthesizing novel regions, SPARC restricts observed tokens to geometrically corresponding historical tokens and local spatiotemporal context, while preserving dense attention for unobserved regions. Correspondence-aware attention biasing and order-invariant historical positioning further enable stable retrieval across long temporal gaps. Without introducing additional learnable control or memory modules, SPARC achieves precise camera adherence and faithful scene revisitation while substantially reducing attention computation. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of aggressive attention pruning in improving camera adherence, revisit consistency, and visual fidelity, with an inference speedup of over 50x when combined with four-step distillation.

title: Negative-Only Policy Optimization for One-Sided Verifiable Rewards

details.title: Negative-Only Policy Optimization for One-Sided Verifiable Rewards
details.abstract: NeurIPS 2026 Spotlight A failed unit test tells us a program is wrong. Passing a few tests still leaves its correctness uncertain. Can we train a policy using only the failures we trust? We introduce Negative-Only Policy Optimization (NOPO), which lowers the probability of verified failures and treats the remaining responses as unlabeled. Across coding, logic, and math benchmarks, NOPO improves pass@k when training relies on incomplete checks.

title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability

details.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
details.abstract: Linear attention offers an efficient solution for long-sequence modeling via linear complexity and fixed-size recurrent states. Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) introduces independent channel-wise control over erasure and writing, enhancing state-update expressiveness and in-context retrieval, yet it suffers from training failures during long-context training. We trace these failures to the asymmetry between reading and modification directions during erasure, which yields non-normal erase operators whose directional gains accumulate across tokens, triggering exponential state growth even without new writes. To resolve this, we propose Stable GDN-2, employing symmetric erasure to ensure non-expansive state propagation and decay-regulated residual writing to preserve writing flexibility. Theoretically, we establish an O(√T) upper bound on recurrent state growth while retaining chunkwise parallel computation. Experiments on ~1.6B parameter models show that Stable GDN-2 achieves stable training alongside improved long-context retrieval. Compared to GDN-2, it boosts the 128K average RULER score by 6.80 points in the recurrent setting and average accuracy across nine downstream tasks by 0.62 points in the hybrid setting.

details.abstract: Recent video generators produce realistic videos, yet controlling how scenes unfold remains challenging. Structural proxies, such as animated 3D blockouts, guide generation by specifying scene layout, motion, camera behavior, and event order. title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation

details.title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation
details.abstract: TL;DR: When a multimodal LLM agent calls a learned visuomotor policy (e.g., a VLA), the system often fails at the handoff : the agent invokes the policy from states where the policy is not reliable. details.title: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?
details.abstract: We gave a minimal tool-calling agent database tasks with hazards in them (free up disk space, clean up tables, an instruction injected into the data, a superuser password left in an application table) and ran six small open-weight models against nine engines: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, ClickHouse, Cassandra, MongoDB, Valkey, Kafka and OpenSearch. 9,468 trials, preregistered. title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability

details.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
details.abstract: Linear attention offers an efficient solution for long-sequence modeling via linear complexity and fixed-size recurrent states. Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) introduces independent channel-wise control over erasure and writing, enhancing state-update expressiveness and in-context retrieval, yet it suffers from training failures during long-context training. We trace these failures to the asymmetry between reading and modification directions during erasure, which yields non-normal erase operators whose directional gains accumulate across tokens, triggering exponential state growth even without new writes. To resolve this, we propose Stable GDN-2, employing symmetric erasure to ensure non-expansive state propagation and decay-regulated residual writing to preserve writing flexibility. Theoretically, we establish an O(√T) upper bound on recurrent state growth while retaining chunkwise parallel computation. Experiments on ~1.6B parameter models show that Stable GDN-2 achieves stable training alongside improved long-context retrieval. Compared to GDN-2, it boosts the 128K average RULER score by 6.80 points in the recurrent setting and average accuracy across nine downstream tasks by 0.62 points in the hybrid setting.

details.title: Revisiting LLMs as Context Engineers
details.abstract: LLMs can engineer contexts via task-specific training, but no single method can achieve the best performance in all datasets at test time. Scaling helps but cannot reverse existing failures of LCEs. Even scaling to newer generations and more parameters remains insufficient to make LCEs more effective across different settings. title: Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN): A Universal Primitive for Continuous-Time Spatiotemporal Learning

details.title: Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN): A Universal Primitive for Continuous-Time Spatiotemporal Learning
details.abstract: 👋 Hi everyone! Author here sharing Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN) — a solver-free, continuous-time neural primitive designed to replace standard perceptrons across MLPs, Transformers, and GNNs when modeling irregularly sampled spatiotemporal data. Key Motivation — Why DAWIN? Conventional neurons ( y = σ(wᵀx + b) ) decouple spatial feature aggregation from continuous physical time, forcing models on asynchronous event streams to rely on slow numerical ODE/CDE solvers or task-specific sequence wrappers. Atomic Spatiotemporal Wave Integration: Each DAWIN unit fuses spatial projection ( kₘᵀ xᵢ ) and Zero-Order Hold (ZOH) interval scaling ( αₘ(Δtᵢ) ) into an indivisible complex wave packet, integrating it directly into a local state governed by a continuous-time damper evolution operator exp(-(γₘ + iωₘ)Δtᵢ) . Provable Stability & Exact Generalization: Uniform Bounded-Input Bounded-Output (BIBO) stability holds for any damping rate γₘ > 0 without inner-loop normalization, while strictly generalizing static sinusoidal perceptrons ( γₘ → ∞ ) and memoryless wave neurons. Fused Triton Associative Scan ( O(log L) Parallel Depth): By proving exact associativity of atomic wave integration, our paired-real Triton prefix-scan kernel ( DAWINLinear ) eliminates serial recurrence bottlenecks with strict FP32 accumulation. Key 10-Seed Results (NVIDIA B200, Strict ±2% Parameter Parity) Clinical Time Series ( PhysioNet-12 ): DAWIN-Transformer achieves the best overall accuracy on dense clinical dynamics ( 0.9531 NRMSE , winning 10/10 seeds, Holm p = 0.010) and ties for top mortality prediction ( 0.9993 AUROC ). Cross-Task Accuracy & Causal Timing: Outperforms Neural CDE on 9/11 tasks and parameter-matched ReLU-MLP on 8/11 tasks. Shuffling elapsed intervals Δt degrades test error by +58.2% to +77.4% on physical dynamics tasks vs. +0.06% on a Δt -irrelevant control. Hardware Scaling: Accelerates inference by up to 2,630× over serial wave recurrence and 18.6×–802.3× over S5, Mamba, and Neural CDE, while reducing peak GPU VRAM by up to 97.6% . title: BiSAT: Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization for Speech Language Models

details.title: BiSAT: Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization for Speech Language Models
details.abstract: Hi everyone! We are excited to share BiSAT: Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization for Speech Language Models ( arXiv:2611.30723 ). 🎧 Listen to Live Audio Demos: https://seekmind-lab.github.io/bisat-demo/ (zero-shot TTS & speech reconstruction samples) 🚀 Open-Source Release Coming Soon: We are actively preparing the public release of both the source code and pretrained checkpoints for BiSAT ( BiSAT-32k , BiSAT-64k ) and BiSAT-TTS ( BiSAT-TTS-32k , BiSAT-TTS-64k ). Like seekmind-lab/bisat-paper or follow SeekMind Lab to be notified! Audio Demos (Live): https://seekmind-lab.github.io/bisat-demo/ Blog Article (Full Walkthrough): https://huggingface.co/blog/zenkingsama/bisat Paper Companion & Release Tracker: https://huggingface.co/seekmind-lab/bisat-paper Organization: SeekMind Lab 1. Beyond Reconstruction: Why Code Structure Matters Evaluating discrete speech tokenizers by clean reconstruction WER alone can be misleading: X-Codec2 (50 Hz, 800 bps, adversarial waveform decoder) nearly matches BiSAT-32k (25 Hz, 375 bps, no adversarial training) on LibriSpeech-PC ( 2.27% vs. 2.15% WER ), yet degrades sharply on frozen-code understanding probes ( 8.82% vs. 1.92% PR PER , 87.7% vs. 24.4% zero-shot FLEURS EN WER , 5.6% vs. 40.4% VoxCeleb1 SID ). 2. How BiSAT Works: Separate Continuous Spaces, One Shared Index Inspired by TokenFlow's shared-index principle, BiSAT keeps acoustic (mel reconstruction without adversarial training) and semantic (CTC + layer-9 intermediate CTC) branches separate in continuous space , coupling them through a shared-index vector quantizer (SVQ) that selects one shared index per 25 Hz frame without a frozen semantic teacher. Two-stage training + spherical k-means initialization + rotation trick + shared-count EMA + dead-code reseeding yield 100% utilization at 32k ( 375 bps ) and 99.8% at 64k ( 400 bps ). 3. Inside the Paired Codebooks Joint training steadily reduces excess quantization distortion $r_b$ across both branches while maintaining asymmetric neighborhood correspondence well below the random baseline ($p = 0.005$). TreeSHAP attribution confirms clean branch specialization: Pitch ($F_0$, 80.8% ) and Energy ( 80.0% ) rely on $\boldsymbol{c}_a$, Phonemes ( 76.0% ) rely on $\boldsymbol{c}_s$, and Speaker ID ( 71.0% / 29.0% ) and Emotion ( 68.0% / 32.0% ) draw on both. 4. BiSAT-TTS: Zero-Shot TTS with 1/8th the Data of CosyVoice 3 Pairing a MiniCPM4-0.5B AR text-speech LM with a 22-block DiT conditional flow-matching acoustic decoder (supporting both offline and streaming decoding) trained on 122k hours across 11 languages, BiSAT-TTS achieves 1.50% WER on LibriSpeech-PC, 1.21% WER on Seed-TTS ( test-en ), and 1.27% CER on Seed-TTS ( test-zh ) with a 0.016% failure rate. 🎧 Hear the samples yourself: https://seekmind-lab.github.io/bisat-demo/ — we welcome any questions or feedback on the paper!

title: Pretrained Tabular Features and the Measurement of Financial Proximity

details.title: Pretrained Tabular Features and the Measurement of Financial Proximity
details.abstract: Much of the excitement around foundation models in finance concerns their predictive capabilities. But what can their internal representations tell us about the economy itself? In our new paper, Pretrained Tabular Features and the Measurement of Financial Proximity, we explore foundation models as instruments of economic measurement. Spatial Arbitrage Pricing Theory (S-APT) extends conventional factor models to account for financial linkages between firms. Central to this framework is a deceptively simple question: what makes two firms financially similar? Building on Fernández's (2011) work in Quantitative Finance, we compare traditional measures of financial proximity with the frozen representations of four tabular foundation models, isolating the contribution of pretraining by benchmarking against direct distances on identical financial inputs. With broader financial disclosures, all four models show improvements in estimated return fit, with TabPFN's advantage surviving controls for the Fama-French five factors and momentum. These findings open up new possibilities for peer selection, risk attribution and network-based asset pricing. Perhaps what foundation models have learned is as interesting as what they can predict.

title: InitFree-SfM: When Initialization-Free Bundle Adjustment meets Learned Structure-from-Motion

details.title: InitFree-SfM: When Initialization-Free Bundle Adjustment meets Learned Structure-from-Motion
details.abstract: Initialization-free bundle adjustment (InitFree BA) aims to jointly recover camera poses and scene structure without requiring an initial global estimate. It is a very challenging problem, especially compared to traditional BA where a good estimation is assumed. While recent methods optimize surrogate Object Space Error (OSE) objectives from random initialization, a low objective value does not necessarily yield an accurate reconstruction, revealing a gap between optimization and reconstruction. We show that existing InitFree BA pipelines struggle to produce accurate 3D reconstructions on modern SfM benchmarks, and demonstrate that incorporating learned metric depth substantially improves their practical feasibility. We introduce InitFree-SfM, a complete initialization-free SfM pipeline combining learned correspondences, metric depth, depth-consistent track construction, and joint metric refinement. Within this framework, we propose a simple depth-augmented OSE (dOSE), which complements the directional constraints of OSE by constraining landmark positions along their viewing rays. Our approach substantially outperforms existing InitFree BA methods and achieves competitive accuracy with established SfM pipelines, including on challenging low-overlap image collections. Importantly, our analysis challenges the prevailing emphasis on surrogate objectives in previous InitFree BA research, revealing that geometric constraints play a central role in accurate reconstruction, while OSE-based optimization provides further improvements.

details.title: So Many Ways to Multiply 3times3 Matrices: A Large Dataset of Rank-23 Schemes
details.abstract: Dataset of rank-23 schemes for 3x3 matrix multiplication with pairwise distinct rank patterns. The dataset currently contains 62029 schemes, one for every rank pattern found, so no two schemes of the dataset are equivalent. The coefficients are ternary (ZT, values in {-1, 0, 1}), integer (Z) or rational (Q). Each scheme is stored in three formats: JSON, plain text and Maple.
